messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: possibly usable reference cvodes implementation
parts:
Hi!

Maybe the cantera project is a good starting point for integrating cvodes into Stan. I think the license allows so and the code looks fairly clean:

https://github.com/Cantera/cantera/tree/2334410b5bd6a576169b56ce8596bce4a55b4541/src/numerics

and

https://github.com/Cantera/cantera/blob/2334410b5bd6a576169b56ce8596bce4a55b4541/src/numerics/CVodesIntegrator.cpp

see there the cvodes integrator classes. Looks like nice code which exposes most major options important for ODE integration and also enables LAPACK when available which should give a decent speedup (2-3x) when enabled.

The license is "new BSD" from the project home:

https://code.google.com/p/cantera/

So it should be good to go into Stan?

Sebastian

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] possibly usable reference cvodes implementation
parts:
Yes, BSD is OK. Overall, though, I'd prefer not to depend on
these intermediate packages. I think the main issue is getting
the builds working everywhere, so I'm not sure we need this kind
of intermediate layer.

Also, this particular one has a C-like interface from C++; I'd
much rather get a proper C++ designed interface.

I'm curious what Daniel or Michael think --- they've spent a lot
of time looking at the Sundials code so have a better idea than me
of what this interface might be contributing.

- Bob
